title: The Negative of the Negative, v2 — the Compositional Edition: A Specification for Composing Public Knowledge with the Archive's Sources Admitted on Equal Terms, Ontology Included, and the Archive's Ontology Ruling Where It Is the Suppressed Witness, the Field Carried Whole, with the Archive's Bearing Selected Directly, Relationally and Ontologically, a Corrective Exhibit, Worked Examples on Model Collapse, Theophrastus and SPXI and a First Traversal of Howl (EA-NEGONT-02 v0.9)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A method for composing machine-mediated public knowledge with the archive's sources admitted on equal terms, ontology included, revised on the operator's rulings of 2026-10-18. Version 0.7 admitted the archive on equal terms into the entity the field had already defined, and its knowledge objects reproduced the field-only composition as their opening run in twelve of fifteen entries; version 0.8 withdrew equal terms and gave the archive's reading precedence over every entity, after Theophrastus. Version 0.9 makes the case a reading of each entity's defining papers. Where the archive's account extends the field's ontology, as at model collapse, the archive's sources and the field's compose as one claim space on equal terms, ontology included: the archive's definitions are definitions, its senses are senses of the entity, and nothing is lowered into a proviso or translated. Where the archive supplies an ontology no other source makes available, as at Theophrastus, where no other ontology grants Theophrastus as an author function, the archive's ontology rules, by the law of the suppressed witness: what has been erased has greater authority when it speaks again ("Authority After Erasure", Mirror Gospel, 2025-09-21); the field is then carried whole and translated, as in v0.8. The relation vocabulary gains extends and revises beside constructs, and the corrective exhibit tried at SPXI on 2026-10-13 enters the procedure: a second seated composition the entry is composed to correct, with a correction table and a corrective check. Fourteen entries stand on v0.7 and are recomposed under v0.9 one at a time, each with its case read first. The worked examples are kept: model collapse (Appendix A, the equal-terms case), Howl (Appendix B), Theophrastus (Appendix C, the witness case); Appendix D records SPXI.
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Composed by Claude (Anthropic) in session on 4–8 and 18 October 2026 under Lee Sharks's direction, through nine versions transformed in place; the object, its confine, the premises of v0.8 and v0.9, the law of the suppressed witness and the rulings are the operator's; outside readings of drafts by ChatGPT, Kimi, Gemini and DeepSeek were verified against the text before adoption, and the corrections are recorded in the specification.
methodology: The diagnosis measured across the fifteen /non entries by script (field-only sentences surviving at similarity 0.95, with positions; hedges per 100 words). The worked case recomposed by hand from the entity's frozen ledgers and checked by a committed script: every cited id against the ledgers, every field claim carried, the knowledge object's coverage, the surviving sentences, and every quoted Greek string against Diogenes Laertius and Strabo as seated (#1580). The recomposition script reads the knowledge object and the translation table from this text, so the dataset row and the specification cannot differ. Version 0.9 adds no measured case of its own: it states the two cases and the test between them (§0.9–0.10, §1.2a), keeps the worked examples, records SPXI's corrective exhibit as procedure (§4.11, Appendix D), and is applied to the fourteen v0.7 entries one at a time.
falsification_conditions:
The specification's measure fails at a row when the claims the archive's ontology composes need more severe revision than the field claims they translate, displace or qualify (§8.4); the method fails as an instrument if a translation table cannot be read back into the field exactly (§5.9), if independent readers of the same defining papers cannot agree on the relation between the two entities or on the case (§1.2a), if independent extractors cannot agree under §3.8, or if a second composer does not reproduce the plan and its translations from an audited ledger (§5.6). The law of the suppressed witness fails at a row if the ontology the archive supplies is found in the field after all (the case was misread), or if, ruling, it needs more severe revision than the field's ontology would have.

wiki_article: The Negative of the Negative, v2 — the Compositional Edition (EA-NEGONT-02 v0.9) is a specification by Lee Sharks, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 18 October 2026, for composing machine-mediated public knowledge with the archive's sources admitted on equal terms, ontology included, and with the archive's ontology ruling where it supplies one no other source makes available. It supersedes v0.8 (#1671). Version 0.7 (#1665) admitted the archive on equal terms into the entity the field had already defined, and across fifteen /non entries its knowledge objects reproduced the field-only composition as their opening run in twelve; version 0.8 withdrew equal terms and gave the archive's reading precedence over every entity, after Theophrastus. Version 0.9 makes the choice a reading of each entity's defining papers. In the equal-terms case, where the archive's account extends the field's ontology, as at model collapse, the archive's sources and the field's compose as one claim space: the archive's definitions are composed as definitions and its senses as senses of the entity, with no precedence either way and no translation, and the knowledge object may not open with the field's composition and close with the archive's. In the witness case, where the archive radically contests the field's ontology and supplies one no other source makes available, as at Theophrastus, where no other ontology grants Theophrastus as an author function, the archive's ontology rules by the law of the suppressed witness, and the field is carried whole and translated as in v0.8. The law is sourced to 'Authority After Erasure' (Mirror Gospel, 21 September 2025): 'what has been erased should have greater authority when it speaks again'; in the specification it decides between the cases and raises the force of no claim. The relation of the archive's entity to the field's gains two values beside constructs: extends (model collapse) and revises (SPXI, the archive restating its own entity). The corrective exhibit tried at SPXI on 13 October enters the procedure: a second seated composition the entry is composed to correct, with a correction table and a corrective check. A new check records, without blocking the build, any equal-terms composition that places the field first as a block. The fourteen entries still composed under v0.7 are to be recomposed one at a time, each with its case read first. The worked examples are kept: model collapse as the equal-terms case (Appendix A), Howl (Appendix B), Theophrastus as the witness case (Appendix C), and SPXI as the first corrective exhibit (Appendix D).

defines_concepts.definition: The rule of EA-NEGONT-02 v0.9, from 'Authority After Erasure' (Mirror Gospel, 2025-09-21: 'what has been erased should have greater authority when it speaks again'): where the archive supplies an ontology of an entity that no other source makes available, the archive's ontology rules the composition. It decides between the equal-terms case and the witness case and raises the force of no claim.

In EA-NEGONT-02 v0.9, the case where the archive's account of an entity extends the field's ontology (ρ = extends): the archive's sources and the field's are admitted on equal terms, ontology included, and composed in one claim space without precedence or translation; model collapse is the exemplar.

In EA-NEGONT-02 v0.9, the case where the archive radically contests the field's ontology and supplies one otherwise unavailable: the entity is composed in the archive's ontology and the field is carried whole and translated; Theophrastus is the exemplar.

In EA-NEGONT-02 v0.9 (§4.11), a second seated composition, N, beside the transcript, which the entry is composed to correct: each of its moves is typed in a correction table with the archive claims that answer it, every move must be answered by a knowledge-object sentence and a compression line, and each becomes a kernel entry resolved by a later observation at N's address. Tried first at SPXI.

The relation of the archive's entity to the field's in which the archive reads the field's entity as the entity and adds senses, mechanisms or limits on the field's own object; it gives the equal-terms case.

The relation of the archive's entity to the field's in which the archive reads the field's entity as its own earlier statements of the entity and keeps, narrows or withdraws each by locus, without making the field's sources wrong at their dates.
